title: 1700 Beats 2300 Master!
informationNeeded: A PGN or complete FEN with side to move and board orientation, or clear full-board frames covering the relevant endgame.
reviewNotes: Physical-board game recap with endgame material, but board visibility and camera angle change. Narration alone does not identify all squares or moves.
transcript: This is me, a 1,700 rated player. And this is my opponent, a 2300 rated candidate master. And I'm kind of laughing here because I know that I stand no chance. And I play my London system, which my opponent is not happy to see because this is considered a boring opening. After a few moves, we start trading pieces in the center, which benefits me because being the less experienced player, there are less chances for me to get outplayed in the middle game like this. But despite having a decent position, I do go on to blunder a fork with the rook. And after this, I'm simply going to lose my knight. But I am here to fight. So I play on and I decide to sacrifice even a rook back to get some more counterplay and complicate the position from my opponent. And my persistence gets rewarded because a few moves later, my opponent plays this move thinking that he's simply going to win. But I have this intermetzo, a check with the queen that gets out of the attack of the rook. And now I'm simply going to win the rook back. He has to cover the check with the queen because of my rook in the back rank. And after this move, I pick up the black rook. So now I'm in a king, pawn, and rook endame with three extra pawns. And I find this move to simplify. And after this, even against a candidate master, there is nothing to do. And the game is simply over. I am going to promote one of my pawns. And so my opponent resigns. And you can see here how happy I am to get my first ever titled
